chapter: Hard times and working bands of the 1930s
title: Trumpeter Andrew Anderson and his break with George Lewis
summary: Rene and Zander discuss Andrew Anderson's playing, his drinking, and his time with George Lewis.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Cause after my brother left there that way, what you call him, got the job, Andrew Anderson? Yeah. That boy's a nice trumpet player, Andrew Anderson.
Does he play like anybody in particular? No, he seems to have a pretty style of his own. But he plays pretty nice, you know that? And he's a powerful trumpet player too.
He can play some pretty stuff real soft too, he can get soft and play pretty.
I'd like to see him get a real good band, man. I think he, and he's a solid nice fella too, you know.
He had a good break with George Lewis.
But I don't know, maybe he has troubles too, you know.

Fella can change, you know, sometimes. Fella can change. I don't know how George Lewis said, George Lewis said, you should be alright fella. And of course sometimes a fella, he'd get swell, you know. Sometimes he'd get to be popular, you see. And you just think that there.
You can do, just go along and make it with anybody, see fit, you know?
Oh no, I didn't mean George. I think Anderson sometimes has a little trouble.
Oh yeah, he might be a little hot-headed. I think he...
No, no, he maybe drinks a little bit.
But that's what I'm talking about. I'm talking about when he gets like that, see? Juggie. Yeah.
